desc: Prove order preservation (pieces never cross, gaps non-increasing, merges permanent) and reduce to ordered group partition; output -1 when count1(A) < count1(B).

Settle reduction: (a) gap constraints + (b) per-piece distance ≤ K characterize reachability; constructive parking/merging argument; m == g case is forced singletons with answer max |s_k − b_k| subject to gap feasibility.
Design near-linear algorithm: binary search on K with greedy leftmost-valid partition check (amortized O(m) per check).
Implement fast I/O solution for T test cases, total N ≤ 1e6, printing per-case answer or -1.
Stress-test current solution vs brute-force simulator on exhaustive/random tiny cases; no mismatches (exhaustive N≤6, random N≤9, plus bitmask-BFS stress at N≤12).
Verify against provided samples (3, -1, 5 confirmed) and edge cases: single piece, A == B, boundary squares, forced-apart impossibility.
